assignedReviews.card_evidence: A woodpecker has strong neck muscles that power its pecking and help keep its head steady.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes internal neck muscles and their role in pecking and keeping the head steady. G3-L-4 specifically targets outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings and their role in movement and gathering food. Neck muscles are not an outer body part, and pecking/head steadiness is not movement or food gathering as intended by the competency.

copy.en:
What powers a woodpecker's strong pecking?

A woodpecker has strong neck muscles that power its pecking and help keep its head steady.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagbibigay-lakas sa pagtuktok ng woodpecker?

May malalakas na kalamnan sa leeg ang woodpecker na nagbibigay-lakas sa pagtuktok nito at tumutulong panatilihing steady ang ulo.
copy.bis:
Unsay naghatag kusog sa pagtuktok sa woodpecker?

Ang woodpecker adunay kusgan nga kaunoran sa liog nga naghatag kusog sa pagtuktok ug nagtabang magpalig-on sa ulo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A worker ant's job changes as it gets older
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes age-based job changes in worker ants, not the stages of an animal life cycle, and does not use a flow chart as required by the competency.

copy.en: A worker ant's job changes as it gets older — young ones care for babies inside the nest, while older ones go outside to find food!
copy.tl: Nagbabago ang trabaho ng worker ant habang tumatanda ito — ang mga bata ay nag-aalaga sa loob ng pugad, at ang matatanda ay lumalabas maghanap ng pagkain!
copy.bis: Mausab ang trabaho sa worker ant samtang motigulang kini — ang batan-on nag-atiman sulod sa salag, ug ang tigulang mogawas mangita og pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The real cause of intestinal worms is worm eggs getting into your mouth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses a health myth about worms, mentioning worm eggs as the cause, but does not explain how interactions between living things (or living/non-living things) bring good or harm. It lacks any instructional content on the interaction concept required by G6-L-8.

copy.en:
Does candy really give you worms?

No! The real cause of intestinal worms is worm eggs getting into your mouth — not candy or sweets.
copy.tl:
Totoo bang nagbibigay ng bulate ang kendi?

Hindi! Ang tunay na sanhi ng bulate ay ang itlog ng bulate na nakakapasok sa bibig — hindi ang kendi.
copy.bis:
Tinuod ba nga maghatag ug bulate ang kendi?

Dili! Ang tinuod nga hinungdan sa bulate mao ang itlog sa bulate nga makasulod sa baba — dili ang kendi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: boiled guava leaves have long been used to wash wounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves but only as a medicinal wash for wounds; it does not address observing outer plant parts or their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: boiled guava leaves have long been used to wash wounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a traditional human use of a plant for wound care, not how living things depend on one another or the environment to meet basic needs.

copy.en: In the Philippines, boiled guava leaves have long been used to wash wounds — studies show they contain compounds that slow germs and help keep a wound clean.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, matagal nang ginagamit ang pinakuluang dahon ng bayabas para maghugas ng sugat — may sangkap ito na pumipigil sa germs, kaya nakakatulong panatilihing malinis ang sugat.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, dugay na gigamit ang gilat-an nga dahon sa bayabas sa paghugas og samad — adunay sulod nga makapugong sa germs, nga makatabang himoong limpyo ang samad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wounds don't heal in one day — they take several days or even weeks to fully close up.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that wound healing takes time. It does not mention cell division, mitosis, meiosis, or the role of mitosis in growth and repair, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Wounds don't heal in one day — they take several days or even weeks to fully close up.
copy.tl: Hindi agad gumagaling ang sugat — umaabot ito ng ilang araw o linggo bago tuluyang gumaling.
copy.bis: Dili dayon mo-ayo ang samad — mokabat kini og pipila ka adlaw o semana una hingpit nga mo-ayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A scab is dried blood that forms a cover to protect your wound while it heals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: A scab as a cover is skin healing, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A scab is dried blood that forms a cover to protect your wound while it heals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: A scab is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en:
What is a scab?

A scab is dried blood that forms a cover to protect your wound while it heals!
copy.tl:
Ano ang langib?

Ang langib ay natuyong dugo na bumubuo ng panakip na nagpoprotekta sa sugat!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang langib?

Ang langib mao ang namala nga dugo nga mahimong taklob nga manalipod sa samad!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A small wound heals faster than a big, deep one.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a general fact about wound healing speed but does not mention cell division, mitosis, meiosis, or the role of mitosis in growth and repair. It shares the concept of repair but provides no instructional support for the competency's specific content.

copy.en: A small wound heals faster than a big, deep one.
copy.tl: Mas mabilis gumaling ang maliit na sugat kaysa sa malaki at malalim.
copy.bis: Ang gamay nga samad mas paspas mo-ayo kay sa dako ug lawom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The very first X-rays were discovered a long time ago, way back in the year 1895!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions X-rays, which is a scientific invention/discovery, but it does not identify any scientist (Filipino or foreign) or their specific invention. The competency requires using secondary sources to identify a scientist and their invention; the card only gives a year and the name of the discovery, so it does not directly support the skill.

copy.en: The very first X-rays were discovered a long time ago, way back in the year 1895!
copy.tl: Ang mga unang X-rays ay natuklasan noong matagal na ang nakalilipas, noong taong 1895!
copy.bis: Ang una nga mga X-rays nadiskobrehan kaniadto, balik sa tuig 1895!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We often yawn when we see someone else yawn, so a yawn can feel like it spreads from person to person.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses contagious yawning, a social behavior, but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Bakit nakakahawa ang paghikab?

We often yawn when we see someone else yawn, so a yawn can feel like it spreads from person to person.
copy.tl:
Bakit nakakahawa ang paghikab?

Madalas tayong humihikab kapag may nakita tayong humihikab, kaya parang kumakalat ito mula sa isang tao papunta sa iba.
copy.bis:
Nganong makatakod ang paghaya?

Sagad ta mohaya kung makita nato nga naghaya ang lain, mao nga morag mikaylap kini gikan sa usa ka tawo ngadto sa lain.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows yeast producing CO2 as evidence of being alive, but the competency specifically requires describing characteristics of living things: grow, respond, and reproduce. The card does not address any of these three characteristics.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions carbon dioxide gas but does not teach the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or identify that matter exists in these states. The gas mention is incidental, not instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies yeast is a living thing, but it does not contrast living vs non-living things or give examples of each. It does not directly support observing and describing the difference between living and non-living things.

copy.en: Feed yeast some sugar and it releases carbon dioxide gas—enough to inflate a balloon on a bottle, proving yeast is alive!
copy.tl: Pakainin mo ng asukal ang lebadura at gagawa ito ng carbon dioxide gas—sapat para magpalobo sa bote, patunay na buhay ang lebadura!
copy.bis: Pakana og asukal ang lebadura ug mohimo kini og carbon dioxide gas—igo na makapahubag sa lobo sa botelya, ebidensya nga buhi ang lebadura!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without air, it makes much more carbon-dioxide gas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions carbon dioxide as a product of yeast activity but does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products in a way that teaches the competency. It is a specific example of fermentation, not a description of respiration.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without air, it makes much more carbon-dioxide gas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It only mentions carbon dioxide as a gas produced by yeast, which is unrelated to the composition of air.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without air, it makes much more carbon-dioxide gas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses gas production by yeast but does not explain bond formation or breaking as constituting a chemical change. It does not address the formation of new substances in terms of chemical bonds.

copy.en:
Why is bread dough covered while rising?

With air, yeast multiplies fast but makes little gas. Without air, it makes much more carbon-dioxide gas — that's why dough is covered while rising.
copy.tl:
Bakit natatakpan ang masa habang umaalsa?

Kapag may hangin, mabilis dumadami ang yeast pero kaunti lang ang gas. Kapag walang hangin, mas marami itong nagagawang carbon-dioxide gas — kaya nakatakip ang masa habang umaalsa.
copy.bis:
Nganong gitabonan ang minasa samtang nag-alsa?

Kung adunay hangin, paspas modaghan ang yeast apan gamay ra ang gas. Kung walay hangin, mas daghan kining mahimong carbon-dioxide nga gas — mao nga tabonan ang minasa samtang nag-alsa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some animals are born already knowing their migration route, while others must learn it by following their parents and remembering the path.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses whether migration routes are inherited or learned, which is about animal behavior and information transfer, not about animals changing to better suit their environment (adaptation) as required by G5-L-9. It does not mention mimicry, camouflage, or any evolutionary change, so it provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: Some animals are born already knowing their migration route, while others must learn it by following their parents and remembering the path.
copy.tl: May mga hayop na namamana ang ruta ng paglalakbay kaya alam na agad ng bata kahit mag-isa; sa iba, natututo ang bata sa pagsunod sa magulang at pag-alala ng daan.
copy.bis: Adunay mga mananap nga napanunod ang ruta sa panaw busa nahibal-an dayon sa bata bisan mag-inusara; sa uban, makakat-on ang bata pinaagi sa pagsunod sa ginikanan ug paghinumdom sa dalan.
